paper_metadata.title: Effects of Ho on the microstructure and mechanical properties of Mg-Zn-Ho-Zr magnesium alloys

evidence.quote: The widely used magnesium alloys belonging to Mg-Zn-Zr (ZK) series, such as ZK60 and ZK61, have excellent deformability, good room-temperature mechanical properties, and low cost.
The microstructure and mechanical properties of Mg-Zn-Ho-Zr alloys have been investigated in detail.

other.master_alloys: pure Mg, pure Zn, Mg-9%Ho, Mg-25%Zr

evidence.quote: The alloys were prepared by melting them in an electrical resistance furnace in a steel crucible under protection of a mixed gas SF6 (1 vol.%) and CO 2 (bal.). Pure Mg was used as a starting material, pure Zn was added during melting, and Ho and Zr were added as master alloys, Mg-9%Ho and Mg-25%Zr, prepared beforehand. The alloys were cast into steel molds.

attributes.composition: Mg3Zn6Y-type icosahedral quasicrystal (reported as found in Mg-Zn-Y alloys)

evidence.quote: As suggested by the XRD patterns, the as-cast alloy contains W-phase and I-phase, which were found in Mg-Zn-Y alloys [8].
EDX microanalyses indicate that most of these compounds are Mg-Zn-Ho ternary phases.
The XRD patterns indicated that I-phase dissolved into the matrix during solution treatment, but W-phase still remained at grain boundaries after solution treatment.

The average grain size of the as-cast Mg-Zn-Ho-Zr alloy is much smaller than that of the as-cast Mg-Zn-Zr alloy. It can be concluded that Ho has great effect on grain refinement of the as-cast Mg-Zn-Ho-Zr alloy.
The eutectic phases along grain boundaries dissolved into the Mg-matrix, and the grains became a little larger in the Mg-Zn-Zr alloy after solution treatment.

However, in the Mg-Zn-Ho-Zr alloy, there were still lots of second phases that remained along grain boundaries, and the average grain size in the solution-treated mi crostructure was almost the same as that of the as-cast alloy.

The amount of the eutectic compounds reduced, and the continuity of the network broke after solution treatment. Eutectic phases in the Mg-Zn-Ho-Zr alloy just partially dissolved into the matrix during solution treatment.
The possible reason is that the grain growth of the Mg-Zn-Ho-Zr alloy during solution treatment was suppressed by the undissolved second phases.
Therefore, the solution strengthening effect and the ageing strengthening effect of the Mg-Zn-Ho-Zr alloy were lower than those of the Mg-Zn-Zr alloy.
As a result, the solubility of Zn in the Mg matrix decrease, and the ageing strengthening effect in the Mg-Zn-Ho alloy weakened correspondingly.

These Mg-Zn-Ho phases cannot completely dissolve into the Mg matrix after solution treatment, as indicated in Figs.1 to 3. There are still lots of Mg-Zn-Ho particles (W-phase) that remained at grain boundaries after solution treatment. As a result, the solubility of Zn in the Mg matrix decrease, and the ageing strengthening effect in the Mg-Zn-Ho alloy weakened correspondingly.

The UTS and YS of both the alloys increased after solution-plus-aging treatment, but the increment of the Mg-Zn-Ho-Zr al-loy was lower than that of the Mg-Zn-Zr alloy.
